blocks.text: Imagine building a house without a blueprint. Just like construction, software development requires precise specifications to ensure successful outcomes.

blocks.markdown: In software development, a formal specification is a detailed description of the behavior a software component must exhibit. It is crucial to distinguish between what a system must do (specification) and how it does it (implementation). This lesson will guide you through writing formal specifications and understanding their importance.

blocks.title: Formal Specification
blocks.text: A formal specification is a mathematically precise description of software behavior, detailing inputs, outputs, and the relationship between them without dictating how the behavior is implemented.

blocks.markdown: Formal specifications serve as a contract between stakeholders, ensuring that the developer understands exactly what is expected. By focusing on 'what' rather than 'how', specifications allow developers the flexibility to choose the most efficient implementation.

blocks.caption: General form of a function specification, mapping inputs to outputs.

blocks.title: Specifying a Simple Function
blocks.prompt: Write a formal specification for a function that takes an integer and returns its square.

steps.text: Define the relationship between input and output.

blocks.markdown: A good specification should not constrain the implementation. This means it should not dictate how the function is computed, only what the result should be. This allows for optimizations and improvements without changing the specification.

blocks.title: Flexibility in Implementation
blocks.text: A specification should describe what a system does, not how it does it, allowing developers to choose the most efficient implementation method.

blocks.title: Ambiguity in Informal Requirements
blocks.prompt: Identify the ambiguity in the following requirement: 'The system should handle user input quickly.'

steps.latex: Quickly \text{ is subjective and lacks a precise definition.}
\text{Specify a maximum response time, e.g., within 200 ms.}

blocks.answer: The term 'quickly' is ambiguous. A precise specification would state a maximum response time, such as 'within 200 ms'.

blocks.markdown: Ambiguities in specifications can lead to misunderstandings and incorrect implementations. Always aim for clarity and precision in your specifications.

blocks.title: Avoiding Ambiguity
blocks.text: Ambiguous specifications can lead to incorrect implementations. Use precise and measurable terms.

points: Formal specifications describe what a system should do, not how.
Clarity and precision in specifications prevent misunderstandings.
